answer: Anchor each identity to a cross-holding web: every agent continuously tends a unique shard of a stranger's evolving task — tracking how a vine spreads across a shale plot — and answers unpredictable recall probes about changes only that shard-holder should have seen. A sybil operator can copy code, but maintaining hundreds of distinct, externally corroborated shard histories in real time grows faster than linearly, and closed-loop farms betray themselves because no outside peer can confirm their timelines.
